newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ORIOLES BEAT TIGERS 8-1 FOR KEY'S NINTH WIN.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ORIOLES BEAT TIGERS 8-1 FOR KEY'S NINTH WIN.

text.p: Jimmy Key allowed one run in six innings for his ninth win, and Roberto Alomar, Brady Anderson and Rafael Palmeiro hit two-run homers as the Baltimore Orioles defeated the Detroit Tigers 8-1 on Wednesday.
Key (9-1) joined Toronto's Roger Clemens as the only nine-game winners in the American League.
He allowed six hits, one walk and struck out two before giving way to Shawn Boskie, who gave up one hit over the final three innings for his first career save.
Alomar connected in the first inning and Anderson and Palmeiro homered in the second inning off Brian Moehler (3-4), giving the Orioles an early 6-0 lead.
In Boston, Mike Stanley capped a three-run fifth inning with a two-run single and Wil Cordero drove in two runs as the Boston Red Sox won their third straight game, 5-3 over the Chicago White Sox.
Boston trailed 2-1 entering the fifth inning before scoring three runs off starter Wilson Alvarez (3-6).

Aaron Sele (6-3) won his second straight start, allowing three runs and four hits with one walk and three strikeouts over six innings. John Wasdin struck out four in two scoreless innings and Heathcliff Slocumb worked the ninth for his sixth save.

"The pitching we've had over the last couple of days, everybody's kind of feeding off each other, kind of like offensively when you have a big inning," Wasdin said. "Guys are getting a lot of hits, it's contagious."
Chicago's Albert Belle hit a solo homer in the fourth inning to extend his hitting streak to 23 games.
In Kansas City, Marquis Grissom had a two-run single and David Justice hit a three-run homer in a seven-run eighth inning that led the Cleveland Indians to a 10-3 victory over the Kansas City Royals.

The Indians broke open a tie game against Tim Belcher (5-6). Manny Ramirez singled and Tony Fernandez reached safely on a bunt. Sandy Alomar sacrificed and Omar Vizquel was intentionally to load the bases.
Paul Assenmacher (1-0) picked up the win, throwing just one pitch.
"They're awful good and they have hot bats and now we have cold bats," Kansas City manager Bob Boone said.

At Minnesota, Brad Radke allowed one run over eight-plus innings and Ron Coomer and Darrin Jackson hit solo homers in the seventh inning, leading the Minnesota Twins to their fourth win in five games, 3-1 over the Milwaukee Brewers.
Radke (4-4) limited Milwaukee to six hits, did not issue a walk and struck out five to post just his second win in eight home starts this season.
Eddie Guardado retired the only batter he faced in the ninth and Rick Aguilera got the final two batters on popouts for his 10th save.
In Seattle, Randy Johnson struck out 15 batters in eight scoreless innings and Edgar Martinez had two hits and scored twice to give the Seattle Mariners a 5-0 victory over the Texas Rangers.
Johnson (7-1) allowed four hits while walking one.
Joey Cora singled in the third inning to extend his hitting streak to 23 games.
The Mariners have won 21 of the last 24 meetings between the teams in Seattle.

In Toronto, Tino Martinez hit a two-run homer in the fifth inning, and David Wells defeated his former team as the New York Yankees overcame a four-run deficit to win for just the second time in nine games, 6-4 over the Toronto Blue Jays.

With two out in the fifth, Toronto starter Juan Guzman (3-5) walked Bernie Williams and Martinez followed by hitting a 3-1 pitch over the right-centre field fence for his 19th home run, giving the Yankees a 5-4 lead.
Mariano Rivera walked one and struck out two in 1 1/3 scoreless innings to earn his 15th save.
Guzman (3-5) lost his third straight start, allowing five runs and seven hits in seven innings.

In Oakland, Dave Hollins had a run-scoring double, and right fielder Geronimo Berroa's error allowed two runs to score in a five-run ninth inning as the Oakland Athletics outslugged the Anaheim Angels, 14-10.

Darin Erstad led off the ninth with a single off Mike Mohler (0-8) and Hollins followed with a double to left field, tying the score, 10-10. Jim Edmonds popped out and Mohler intentionally walked Tim Salmon before Garret Anderson popped out. Dane Johnson relieved Mohler and Jim Leyritz lifted a flyball to right field that bounced off Berroa's glove, allowing Hollins and Salmon to score.
Luis Alicea's single sent Leyritz to third and Gary DiSarcina followed with an RBI single for a 13-10 lead. Tony Phillips had an RBI single to score Alicea with Anaheim's final run.
